## Highlights since 0.19.4

- **Lattice on the Mac is now the native app.** From this update, every Mac runs the native Lattice, drawn by the Mac's graphics hardware instead of a web page, on Apple silicon and on Intel Macs alike. It looks and works the way Lattice does, and it is faster and lighter. Updating installs it in place of the classic version, with nothing to choose. Your recent projects, settings, themes, plugins, project templates, Agent skills, Agent conversations and Overleaf links come with you. If you had switched back to the classic version, what you changed there since comes along too: the projects you opened, the settings you changed there (a setting the native version already held at a value of its own, one it brought over from the classic version included, keeps that value), and the themes, plugins, templates and skills you added. Typst support downloads again the first time you build a Typst document. The native version has no grammar check and no dictionaries for other languages; spell check uses macOS's own checker. Windows and Linux keep the classic version.
- **No more switching back.** Settings › Editor & builds no longer offers to switch back to the classic version. The classic version's data stays on your Mac, untouched.
- **VS Code colours for code, and a code theme you choose.** VS Code's Light+ and Dark+ colours are the new default code theme. A code theme you chose stays as it is, and a copy that already ran the native version keeps GitHub, the earlier default: choose VS Code under Settings › Appearance › Code theme to switch, or GitHub, Weft & Warp, One, Solarized, Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Nord or Monokai. A code block in the visual editor follows the same code theme, so a .py file and a Python block in a note have the same colours. Selecting text in a code block no longer paints the block's padding.
- **A new manuscript inside an open project.** In the native Lattice, New manuscript from template… adds a paper from a venue template or one of your saved templates to a folder of the project you have open, without making a new project. It is on a folder's right-click menu, the Project panel's + and ⋯ menus, and the command palette. New project now asks for the parent folder and shows the folder it will create (#1259).
- **The Agent takes any file.** In the native Lattice, drop any file from the Finder on the Agent, such as a Word document or a spreadsheet, and it is attached to your message (#1254).

## Notable fixes

- In the native Lattice, an installed theme's syntax colours now colour .tex, .py and Typst sources, instead of the code theme's (#1268).
- In the native Lattice, going back to a project that hasn't changed shows its PDF straight away, without building it again (#1267).
- Double-clicking a minted code block in the PDF jumps to that line of your .tex source, instead of opening minted's cache file (#1263, #1266).
- In the native Lattice, a file dragged out of the Project panel into the documents opens there reliably.
